title: The Life-Changing Science of Detecting Bullshit

questions.q: What distinguishes bullshitting from lying according to the book?
a: Disregarding obvious truth rather than deliberately deceiving
Lying involves emotional manipulation while bullshitting does not
Bullshitting requires prior knowledge of the truth
Lying is always more harmful than bullshitting
questions.why: The overview defines bullshitting as disregarding the truth, not as a form of lying.

questions.q: What is the first reason people fall for bullshit?
a: It matches their existing beliefs and memories
They are under time pressure to respond
The speaker uses confident body language
They have no prior knowledge of the topic
questions.why: The three-reasons lesson lists alignment with existing beliefs as the first cause.

questions.q: What example does the book use to show how intuition can mislead?
a: People who believed a Ponzi scheme would make them millionaires
A student who trusted a professor's unverified research
A doctor who ignored symptoms of a rare disease
A parent who dismissed a child's warning about danger
questions.why: The intuition lesson cites Ponzi scheme believers whose gut told them they'd become millionaires.

questions.q: According to Harry Frankfurt, when are people most likely to bullshit?
a: When they are required to give an opinion on a subject
When they are in a familiar social setting
When they feel emotionally threatened
When they are speaking to experts in the field
questions.why: The Frankfurt lesson states people bullshit when required to share an opinion.

questions.q: What additional factor makes people bullshit even more?
a: Talking to people less knowledgeable in the field
Being in a high-stakes professional environment
Feeling anxious about being judged
Having recently been contradicted publicly
questions.why: The Frankfurt lesson notes we bullshit more when talking to less knowledgeable people.
